subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should failure-driven skill repair and usage-based skill retirement live in OpenClaw core/Skill Workshop, in a plugin or ClawHub package using existing hooks and diagnostics, or as a small core API extension first?
rationale: The request adds new config, persisted metrics, failure-context capture, and user skill archive/delete behavior; existing hooks and diagnostics cover part of the telemetry story but not the product policy.

options.title: Design minimal core API first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the smallest approved skill usage, repair, retirement, redaction, and approval contract before implementation is split into phases.

options.title: Prototype as plugin or ClawHub package
options.body: Use `agent_end`, `before_tool_call`, `after_tool_call`, and `skill.used` diagnostics for analytics first, then open a narrow core API gap only if the plugin cannot express the workflow.

options.title: Decline core lifecycle automation
options.body: Close or narrow the issue if maintainers decide automatic skill repair and retirement policy should remain outside OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Design minimal core API first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the smallest approved skill usage, repair, retirement, redaction, and approval contract before implementation is split into phases.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the related suggestion-tier merge that scoped the remaining self-reflection work and has the clearest recent product-history signal for Skill Workshop direction.
